games.reason: Both chains rely on in-vitro predictions and lack variant-centered ChIP support. ZNF696 has a more discriminating predicted allelic difference (alt 95.1 vs ref 21.9 percentile), while TFAP2E’s predicted difference is less pronounced (ref 97.4 vs alt 70.8); TFAP2A and TFAP2C are also expressed, leaving the AP-2 member less resolved. Expression of ZNF696 and TFAP2E is otherwise comparable, so this is a modest advantage, not direct evidence of occupancy or regulation.

The evidence does not separate the chains. Both have an in-vitro model predicting the stated allele preference (TFAP2E favors ref; ZNF696 favors alt), and both TFs have similar HCT 116 expression (8.5 vs 8.3 TPM). There is no matched-biosample ChIP-seq support for either; the additional ZNF696 assay information is from elsewhere and its lack of a ReMap peak is explicitly not evidence against binding. Their element, gene, and phenotype links are likewise shared and unestablished.
